The binding walk's level-triggered ADOPT arm (binding_walk._adopt_stands_down) already replays exactly this orphan: a lone rebar-id marker equal to the deterministic inbound id, no binding, no local ticket. My reproduction used a 1-binding store, so the blast-radius breaker refused that ADOPT (1/1 > 0.10) on every pass. Measured: with 1 and 9 confirmed bindings the orphan is held (breaker refuses; logged as binding_walk_breaker_refused); with 20 it is imported on the next pass with one CREATE, a binding, no create_issue and a single label, and later passes make no writes. Production has 5953 confirmed bindings, so a failed pass would need more than 595 orphaned imports before the breaker holds them, and holding is the breaker's designed, logged behaviour. Also measured: inbound applies before outbound, so a refused inbound write ends the pass before any outbound Jira write, and plain inbound changes are re-applied next pass. Conclusion: delayed, not lost or duplicated. The fix in this plan is not needed (it would also bypass the breaker). The premise is false; the proof lands as a test under feministic-baboonish-snake, and this bug closes not_a_bug citing it.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

A reconciler pass that fails after an inbound create has written its Jira identity markers permanently loses that Jira issue's import when the pass's uncommitted files are discarded. This is how the production bridge runs: `_bridge_runner.run_bridge` commits and pushes only after a successful pass, and each run starts from a fresh checkout. A reclaim fetched mid-pass (refusal `SupersededStoreRefused` at `finalize_event`) is one way to fail the pass there; any exception does the same.

## Cause (reproduced)

Reproduced at a99339e8ce8 with the stateful fake Jira from `tests/integration/reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py` (one bound pair DIG-1, committed tracker; then a new Jira issue DIG-2 and a Jira rename of DIG-1; the pass's inbound EDIT write raises):

- `applier.apply` applies inbound mutations before outbound ones, so the refusal ends the pass before any outbound Jira write. Plain inbound changes (DIG-1's rename) are only delayed: the next pass imports them, with no Jira writes.
- `apply_inbound._apply_inbound_create` writes CREATE/STATUS, records the binding, then `_inbound_create_writeback_jira` adds label `rebar-id:jira-dig-2` and entity property `local_id` on DIG-2. Those Jira writes land; the local CREATE and binding stay uncommitted.
- After the failed pass's uncommitted files are discarded, DIG-2 is never imported (5 later passes: no local ticket, no binding, no Jira writes). With the files kept (a persistent clone), the next pass converges. The same loss follows a `RuntimeError` at that point, so the reclaim is one trigger of a general defect.
- Why it sticks: `differ._compute_mutations_emit_jira_only` suppresses the inbound create for any issue carrying a `rebar-id:` label ("owned by binding-aware differs"), and `reconcile_helpers.drop_snapshot_differ_property_bound_emissions` drops it for any issue carrying a `local_id` property; but `inbound_differ.compute_inbound_mutations` skips unbound issues. An issue whose inbound import never became durable falls through every differ.

## Approach

Recover the orphaned inbound import at its source, in the reconciler's diff phase, without weakening the suppressions that stop outbound-origin issues being re-imported (bug unaware-subwealthy-pintail):

- New `reconcile_helpers.recover_orphaned_inbound_creates(mutations, ctx)`, called in `run_differs.run_differs` right after the 2 drop filters. For each key new in `ctx.curr_snapshot` relative to `ctx.prev_snapshot` (the same edge the snapshot differ uses for `jira_new`) with no inbound create already in `mutations`, emit the differ's `jira_new` inbound create only when all hold:
  - every identity marker on the issue (`rebar-id:`/`rebar-id-` labels and the `local_id` property, where present) names exactly the deterministic inbound id `inbound_translate._jira_key_to_local_id(key)`, so the marker proves an inbound-origin import (an outbound-origin ticket has a local id of its own);
  - the binding store has no binding for that local id or key, active or retired;
  - no directory for that local id exists in the tracker (a deleted or archived ticket keeps its directory).
- The re-run inbound create is idempotent on Jira: it targets the existing issue (no `create_issue`), and re-adding the same label and property leaves them unchanged.
- Provenance reason `jira_orphaned_inbound_import`, so the recovery is visible in RECON/manifest output.
- No new config key, env var or flag.

## Scope

In: `src/rebar/reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py`, `src/rebar/reconciler/run_differs.py`, new `tests/integration/reconciler/test_inbound_import_survives_failed_pass.py`. Out: making the inbound writeback itself transactional with the local commit (delivery is a separate process step); outbound-origin issues, whose recovery already relies on the `local_id` property (unaware-subwealthy-pintail).

## Testing

New module on the stateful fake Jira and the committed-tracker setup above:
- refusal (`SupersededStoreRefused`) after DIG-2's writeback, pass state discarded: the next pass imports DIG-2 as `jira-dig-2`, bound to DIG-2, with DIG-1's rename applied; Jira gets no `create_issue` and DIG-2 keeps exactly one `rebar-id:` label; a further pass makes no Jira writes and no new local events. Fails on a99339e8ce8.
- same with a `RuntimeError` instead of the refusal.
- guards, each with the marker on the issue and no binding: a marker naming another local id (outbound-origin) is not imported; a tombstoned local `jira-dig-2` directory is not resurrected; a retired binding for DIG-2 is not re-imported.
- persistent clone (pass state kept): converges as today with no duplicate CREATE events.

Existing reconciler suites (`tests/integration/reconciler/`, `tests/unit/reconciler/`) stay green, then `make verify`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When a reconciler pass fails after an inbound create's Jira writeback and the pass's uncommitted state is discarded, the next pass imports that Jira issue locally and binds it; a regression test proves it for a mid-pass reclaim refusal and fails on a99339e8ce8.
- [ ] The recovery makes no `create_issue` call and adds no duplicate identity label; a later pass makes no Jira writes and no new local events for the issue.
- [ ] An identity marker naming a different local id, a deleted (tombstoned) local ticket, and a retired binding are each left alone, proven by tests.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.
